findings.plain_summary: OPM's 60-day notice seeks comment on a new FEHB Protection Act Portal, an enrollee notification and eligibility verification system for family members under the FEHB Protection Act of 2025. The notice estimates about 2.7 million respondents at 30 minutes each, or 1.4 million hours, and says the portal will first serve enrollees whose family members' eligibility is unverified, with employing agencies, payroll offices, and carriers added in later phases.

items.headline: Portal purpose: audit of family-member eligibility under the FEHB Protection Act
items.what_changes: The portal is described as the system through which OPM carries out a statutory requirement to conduct a comprehensive audit of family members covered under FEHB, with the stated goal of ensuring only eligible individuals are enrolled.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The FPA Portal is an enrollee notification and eligibility verification system that will support the OPM requirement under the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Protection Act of 2025 (Sec. 90101, Pub. L. 119-21, 139 Stat. 362) to conduct a comprehensive audit regarding family members who are covered in the FEHB Program.

items.headline: Enrollees with unverified family members get emails and mailed notices
items.what_changes: Enrollees whose family member's eligibility has not been verified receive portal-generated emails and mailed notices directing them to sign in and provide documentation supporting eligibility.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Enrollees whose family member's eligibility has not been verified will receive FPA Portal generated emails and mailed notices.

items.headline: Automated review decides sufficiency; unresolved cases go to a vendor and OPM
items.what_changes: The portal uses automated document verification to decide whether a submission is sufficient to support an eligibility decision. Cases the automated process cannot resolve are referred to the contracted vendor and OPM, and results are returned to the portal.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The FPA Portal will use automated document-verification capabilities to review the submitted information and documentation and determine whether the submission is sufficient to support an eligibility decision.

items.headline: Burden estimate: about 2.7 million respondents and 1.4 million hours
items.what_changes: OPM estimates about 2.7 million respondents, each spending 30 minutes, for a total of 1.4 million burden hours, with annual frequency.
items.speaker: OPM

items.headline: Rollout is phased; agencies, payroll offices, and carriers come later
items.what_changes: The initial phase involves enrollees whose family member's eligibility has not been verified, OPM personnel, and a contracted vendor. Employing agencies, payroll offices, and participating carriers are to be added in subsequent phases.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Employing agencies, payroll offices, and participating health insurance carriers will be incorporated in subsequent phases.

items.headline: Required documents depend on the family member's relationship
items.what_changes: The documents enrollees must upload depend on the family member's relationship to the enrollee and include records used to establish a spouse's or child's eligibility. The full list is in the FEHB Handbook.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The documents required depend on the family member's relationship to the enrollee and include records used to establish a spouse's or child's eligibility.

items.headline: Comment deadline is December 18, 2026
items.what_changes: Comments on the 60-day information collection request are accepted until December 18, 2026, under 5 CFR 1320.8(d)(1).
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Comments are encouraged and will be accepted until December 18, 2026.

could_not_determine: How many enrollees have family members whose eligibility is unverified, and how that population relates to the ~2.7 million respondent estimate
The specific eligibility criteria and the full list of required documents for each family-member relationship (the notice points to the FEHB Handbook)
What happens to an enrollee's FEHB coverage or enrollment if documents are not submitted or verification fails, and the deadlines for response
The criteria the automated document-verification step uses to decide sufficiency, and how often cases are referred to the vendor or OPM
Privacy, data-security, and records protections for the uploaded documents, including whether a system of records notice applies
The identity of the contracted vendor, its contract value, and the government's cost to build and operate the portal
The basis for the 30-minute-per-respondent burden estimate and the 'Affected Public' category of 'eligible individuals or household members'
Timing and scope of the later phases involving employing agencies, payroll offices, and carriers
Whether OPM has received any comments so far, and whether the notice is tied to any specific deadline in the statute
